subject: Piloting compliance credits and HSM licensing—scope vs timing
messages:
From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@stellarhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on scope/timing for compliance fees and HSM licensing

Hi Karthik,

Thank you for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We want to start defining commercial terms for a 3-month pilot followed by a regional rollout. A few open questions from procurement/legal:

- We see several compliance line items in the SOW (audit log ingestion, residency setup, HSM seat license). Can you confirm which items are one-time implementation fees vs recurring?
- StellarHealth is asking whether a portion of the one-time implementation can be converted to a deferred credit that offsets the first 6–12 months of consumption. Is that something Redwood will consider?
- For HSM: we need to understand tradeoffs between annual HSM seat licensing vs billing HSM-related crypto operations as usage-throughput. Which approach do you recommend for pilot-to-scale economics?

Attaching our initial SOW and a rough PO estimate so you can see numbers on our side (StellarHealth_SOW_v1.pdf; PO_estimate.xlsx).

Can we get a short note with options and a proposal by EOD tomorrow? Would prefer a short bulleted comparison so procurement can circulate internally.

Best,
Amanda
Amanda Lee
Director, Procurement — StellarHealth
[a] +1 415-555-0189


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on scope/timing for compliance fees and HSM licensing

Amanda — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. Quick summary up front, then two concrete options for procurement to review:

Summary (short):
- Audit logging and residency infra are typically implemented as an onboarding/setup fee plus a small recurring support/sla charge. HSM can be structured either as an annual seat (fixed) or metered crypto operations (variable). Both have tradeoffs for accounting and scale.

Option A — Amortized onboarding credits (recommended for pilots)
- One-time implementation fee is invoiced at kickoff but 60% is returned as time-bound credits applied against usage for the first 12 months.
- HSM: provision an annual seat for the pilot to simplify ops; we can prorate month-of-onboarding and then re-evaluate at renewal.
- Pros: neat P&L treatment for StellarHealth, faster legal signoff; Redwood bears near-term unit economics risk but recovers over committed usage window.
- Cons: Redwood exposure if pilot doesn’t convert.

Option B — Deferred invoicing + usage surcharge (preferred for longer-term commits)
- Defer 50% of onboarding until 6 months in (invoice milestone), remaining 50% converted to recurring credit against committed reserved capacity.
- HSM: bill HSM crypto ops as usage for the pilot to keep initial OPEX low; on scale, switch to a seat model if predictable.
- Pros: aligns cashflow and reduces Redwood risk; keeps upfront opex low for StellarHealth.

Numbers: I’ve looped in Ben to draft two numeric illustrations (30/60/90 day pilots -> 6/12 month credits) and Mina for contract language for a credit schedule and fallback if pilot fails to convert. See our working breakdown (Drive link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2priceMD

Next steps:
- Ben: can you send the two editable pricing scenarios and a simple MAP (mutual action plan) that procurement can attach to the PO?
- Mina: can you draft a short clause for the contract that captures the credit amortization and cancellation fallback?

Amanda — happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow if that’s easier to align quickly.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on scope/timing for compliance fees and HSM licensing — pricing illustrations attached

Amanda — attaching the numbers per Karthik’s options (pricing_breakdown.xlsx). High level:

- Pilot (3 months) estimate: one-time onboarding $48,000 (covers audit log pipeline, residency config, initial attestation work).
- Option A (amortized credits): 60% ($28,800) invoiced then returned as credits spread over 12 months against usage; remaining $19,200 stays as non-refundable implementation revenue.
- Option B (deferred invoicing): 50% ($24,000) invoiced at kickoff, 50% invoiced at 6 months unless pilot converts to a 12-month reserved commit, in which case we apply a delta credit back to StellarHealth.

HSM recommendation for pilot:
- We suggest annual seat for the pilot but prorated for the pilot months. If you need to keep cashflow low, we can bill HSM crypto ops at $0.0008/op during the pilot and convert to a seat at renewal with a one-time credit to offset pilot ops charges.

Commercial concession: if StellarHealth signs a 12-month reserved capacity agreement within 30 days of pilot kickoff, Redwood will provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the onboarding fee (applied as additional credits over 6 months).

I’ve also thrown together a brief MAP for review — MAP_draft.docx. If the high-level numbers look reasonable, I’ll formalize a line-item SOW and send to finance for a draft invoice schedule.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Karthik / Ben — thanks, that’s helpful and aligned with our internal ask. Two quick asks before we circulate:

1) Please convert Option A and B into a one-page comparison table (cost timing / legal risk / impact to month 1 cashflow). Procurement wants side-by-side to circulate.
2) Can you add the proposed clause language for credits (Mina) so we have one doc to hand Legal?

We’re comfortable moving forward with a 3-month pilot under the amortized-credit approach (Option A) pending final MAP and credit clause. I’ll have procurement route a provisional PO next week so we can hit kickoff the week of May 6.

Amanda
Amanda Lee
Director, Procurement — StellarHealth

Replying briefly to confirm: proceeding with Option A pilot pending MAP + legal language.
